incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — PD#987654 — Hosted-inference cluster us-west-2: increased 5xx rate > 8% over 1m; severity: high. Primary on-call: Alex K. Auto-escalation window: 3m. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-987654
PagerDuty: Notification sent to Alex K (primary). Escalation policy: hosted-inference-prod -> secondary -> manager.
Alex K: ack
Alex K: I see the page, I'm on it. pulling logs now.
Jamal S: @Alex K ping — are you able to access the monitoring dashboard? I can jump in if you need a hand.
Alex K: dashboard loads for me. seeing a sharp rise in 5xx coming from model-serving pods in gw-deploy-2. postfix errors in frontend too.
SRE Ops: copying runbook snippet: ```# runbook: hosted inference 5xx spike
1) check pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-serving
2) check proxy 502/504: kubectl logs proxy-xyz -c envoy
3) scaleup: kubectl scale deploy gw-deploy --replicas=8
4) if degraded, failover traffic to us-east-1 via routing flip
```
Alex K: running step 1 now. recent pod oom/killed on node g4dn-12. looks like a bad batch size causing OOM. logs show "CUDA out of memory" during large-batch inference.
Maria P: @PagerDuty note — primary acked but says they need assistance, PD will auto-escalate if no update in 3m. I'm standing by.
PagerDuty: No update from Alex K at 3 minutes — escalating to secondary (Jamal S).
Jamal S: ack
Jamal S: I'm live. Can confirm OOMs on gw-deploy-2. Node-level memory pressure shows multiple high-alloc processes. I can attempt a rolling restart of affected pods.
Alex K: thanks — I started a small config patch to clamp batch size for that model (`MAX_BATCH=8`) and pushed to canary.
SRE Ops: be careful — canary will only hit small percentage. For immediate relief, suggest scaling replica count + cordon the problematic node. Commands: `kubectl cordon g4dn-12 && kubectl drain g4dn-12 --ignore-daemonsets`
Jamal S: doing drain now. `kubectl drain g4dn-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — draining.
incidentbot: Automated event: node g4dn-12 marked SchedulingDisabled.
Jamal S: drain completed, pods relocated, scaling gw-deploy to 10 replicas.
Maria P: traffic drop in errors down to 3% — nice. still seeing occasional retry storms from queued requests.
Alex K: can we enable prefix KV caching for that model to reduce backend load? I have a patch but need to toggle via feature flag: `FEATURE_CACHE_PREFIX=true` on config map `model-configs/retina-v2`.
Liam (manager): added to thread — I'm awake. Do we have customer-facing impact? Which customers are seeing degraded latency/errors?
Jamal S: quick customer impact check: 2% of overall hosted customers hit errors above 1xx failures; one large customer (acme-pay) reported degraded throughput in the last 10m. I just opened a support ticket with basic details.
Maria P: support ticket #SUP-4321 created and linked into PD incident. Notified account lead.
PagerDuty: Escalation timer expired — manager paging (Liam (manager)). Notification sent.
Liam (manager): ack. thanks for the summary. good mitigation so far. prefer manual confirmation before full traffic flip. @Alex K @Jamal S what's ETA to stable?
Alex K: after clamp + node drain + scale + cache toggle, should be stable in ~6 minutes as in-flight retries clear. I've queued a config patch to flip `FEATURE_CACHE_PREFIX=true` immediately after CI check.
Jamal S: confirming config applied to canary, may roll to 30% in 2m then 100%. I'll hold 100% until Liam gives thumbs.
Liam (manager): agree. keep canary at 30%. prepare a rollback plan. Also, we need to run post-incident notes: assign lead and follow-up actions.
Maria P: noted — I'll create the incident ticket in JIRA with preliminary timeline and customer impact.
Alex K: small hiccup — one of the controller replicas failed to restart due to stale secret mount (k8s error: "secret not found"). I'm patching to reattach secret from `infra-secrets/serving-token`.
SRE Ops: if secret rotation is blocking, use `kubectl set env deployment/controller SERVING_TOKEN=$(kubectl get secret infra-secrets -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d)` as emergency patch.
Jamal S: config toggle to 30% canary done. errors trending down to 1.2%. in-flight queue clearing.
Liam (manager): thanks. @Maria P please ping customer success on acme-pay with an ETA and mitigation note. Keep PD incident open until we hit <0.5% 5xx for 15m.
Maria P: pinged CS and account team. Draft message posted to ticket. cc: @account-team.
incidentbot: PD#987654 status update: acknowledged by primary and secondary; manager paged. Mitigation in progress; monitoring threshold: <0.5% 5xx for 15m to resolve.
Alex K: secret attached, controller coming up. traffic steady. I'll monitor for next 20m.
Jamal S: I'll stay on call for 30m and then handoff to next oncall.
Liam (manager): great work team. After stability, add action items: better batch-size guards, safer secret rotation checks, and an automated node pressure alert. I'll own the postmortem assignment.
Maria P: will file follow-ups. tentative postmortem meeting tomorrow 11am PT.
Alex K: thumbs up. closing note: the immediate root cause looks like an unguarded model update that allowed runaway batch sizes on a specific node type. we'll backfill safeguards.
Jamal S: closing out my active tasks. switching pager to snooze.
incidentbot: PD#987654 resolved at 1845556690 — all thresholds met. Incident log archived.
Liam (manager): marking as monitored. will check postmortem notes tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
